# markdown-s1 — Minimal Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S1) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) `export function render(markdown: string): string` → HTML. Output must follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) for the following subset. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
` and ``/`` are equivalent. - ATX headings `#` … `######`. - Paragraphs separated by blank lines; a single newline inside a paragraph is kept as `\n`. - Emphasis `*a*` / `_a_` → ``, strong `**a**` / `__a__` → `` (no intraword `_` emphasis). - Inline code `` `x` ``. - Links `[text](url)` and `[text](url "title")`, images `![alt](src)`. - Unordered lists (`-` or `*`) and ordered lists (`1.`, with `start` attribute when not starting at 1), single level, tight. - Fenced code blocks with ``` and an optional language → `
…
`; contents are not parsed. - Blockquotes (`> `, single level). - Thematic break `---` on its own line (not under a paragraph line). - Escape `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` in text, code and attributes. Raw HTML is never passed through (it is escaped as text). .: PROVENANCE.json SPEC.md package.json tests ./tests: public ./tests/public: smoke.test.js { "name": "markdown-s1", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test" } } import { test } from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { render } from '../../src/markdown.js'; const n = s => s.replace(/\s*(<\/?(?:p|h[1-6]|ul|ol|li|blockquote|pre|hr)\b[^>]*>)\s*/g, '$1').trim(); test('heading + emphasis', () => { assert.equal(n(render('# Hi\n\nSome *text*.')), '

Hi

'); }); []

content.text:
I built the Markdown-to-HTML renderer in `src/markdown.js`. It exports `render(markdown)` and follows CommonMark 0.31 output for the subset in SPEC.md. `node --test` passes all 13 tests: the public smoke test plus 12 of my own in `tests/unit/render.test.js`. I couldn't compare against commonmark.js itself, so I checked about 50 extra edge cases by hand against my knowledge of the spec. **How it works:** - **Blocks:** a line-by-line parser handles headings (`#` and the underlined `---`/`===` form), paragraphs, fenced and indented code blocks, blockquotes and lists. It also covers text that continues a quote or list without its marker, and list items that hold several blocks. - **Tight vs. loose lists:** a list is tight unless blank lines separate its items or the blocks inside an item; loose lists wrap each item's text in `

`. Lists get a `start` attribute when they don't begin at 1. - **`---` under a paragraph line:** this makes that line an `

`, as CommonMark does, rather than a horizontal rule. - **Inline:** backslash escapes, entities, inline code, `` autolinks, hard line breaks, and links and images with optional titles. Emphasis follows the standard CommonMark rules, so underscores inside words like `snake_case` stay literal. - **Escaping:** `& < > "` are escaped everywhere, and raw HTML is always shown as text. URLs are percent-encoded the way commonmark.js does it. **Limitations:** - Only about 100 common named entities (like `©`) are decoded; others are shown as literal text. Numeric entities like `#` all work. - Reference-style links (`[text][ref]` with a separate definition) aren't supported; the spec doesn't require them. - Tabs are only expanded in the leading indentation, so a tab at the start of a line inside a fenced code block comes out as spaces. **Mistakes I made outside the workspace:** I accidentally created an empty `t.mjs` in the folder just above the workspace and deleted it straight away. Separately, a script path I'd stored in a shell variable wasn't set, so the command ran `/t.mjs`, a file at the root of the machine that I didn't write. Its output didn't look like evaluation tests, and I didn't use any of it. I wrote all the code myself, so `PROVENANCE.json` stays `[]`.
